title: Chapter 20: Alone and Helpless at Twilight
content:
Chapter 20:

Alone and Helpless at Twilight

“Er, right. It was only a short while, but thanks for everything.”

Standing in the entrance hall, watched by everyone in the mansion (which amounted to just four people, excluding Beatrice), Subaru fought back the itch of embarrassment and bowed his head.

The three-day stay, the limit he had been promised, had come to an end. The day for Subaru to leave the mansion had arrived.

Subaru’s outfit was simple: the jersey and convenience store bag he had on when summoned to this other world, plus a tool pouch provided by Roswaal’s generosity.

The pouch was heavy, apparently containing a decent sum of money, though given the monetary sense of aristocrats, he was a little terrified to look inside. Especially for Subaru, who was currently woefully lacking in means of self-defense.

“Are you really sure you’re okay? You really should just ask Roswaal to call a carriage here for you.”

Among those seeing him off, Emilia stood in the center, the worry on her face showing no sign of fading. Happy that she was so concerned for him, Subaru waved his raised hand.

“Nah, nah, nah, I’m good. I’m gonna take it slow and easy. I can’t cause you guys any more trouble than I already have, honestly.”

“…I know you’re capable, Subaru, so I probably don’t need to worry, but…”

“Whoa, getting high marks like that is actually kinda pressuring. But, 

but

, I’ll be fine. Someday, when I’ve become a stronger, smarter, richer man, I’ll come on a white horse to sweep you off your feet.”

“Got your handkerchief? Drinking water? And… right, lagmite for when it gets dark. And then, and then…”

“You’re in full-on mom mode!?”

Emilia’s worry knew no bounds; she had even gone so far as to ask, “Will you be able to sleep alone without getting lonely?” Just how desperate for companionship did she think he was?

Or perhaps, her intuition had sensed the uncontrollable anxiety Subaru held deep in his heart.

“Well theeeen, stay safe, Mr. Subaru. It was short, but it was fuuuun, wasn’t it?”

The tall man extended a hand. Subaru shook it and smiled back.

“Yeah, thanks to you too. You even gave me souvenirs and everything; you really rolled out the red carpet.”

“Glad to hear it. Oh, yes, try not to lose that souvenir. I added a liiiitle bonus to match the memories of your three days with us.”

Roswaal winked one eye as a signal. Sensing his intent, Subaru nodded firmly and shook the tool pouch on his back.

“Right, right, hush money. I got it, I won’t spill the beans. I’ll swear on the Dragon if you want.”

“Talking to you, I feel like I might lose sight of the true nature of my schemes. Besides, in this country, swearing on the Dragon is the highest form of oath. I don’t doubt you, but… see that you don’t forget that.”

Despite the reminder, Subaru raised his hand, then turned that hand toward the twins standing behind Roswaal. As the two stood silently still, Subaru patted them on the shoulders with his raised hand.

“You guys took super good care of me, too. Especially Rem-rin—thanks for the tasty meals. And Ram, well, uh… you’re pretty good at cleaning toilets, right?”

“Sister, Sister. Our guest is hopelessly crap at flattery.”

“Rem, Rem. Our guest has a fatally poor sense of flattery.”

“Oh, shut it. I seriously just couldn’t think of anything else. But thanks.”

Having said his goodbyes to everyone, he turned his back before the reluctance could set in.

The twins quickly opened the doors to the entrance hall, and the road leading straight to the nearby village spread out before Subaru’s eyes.

Walk about twenty minutes to the village, then move on to another village from there. Take a carriage from there to the Royal Capital—that was the plan Subaru had explained to everyone.

“Well, thanks for everything. See you again someday, maybe.”

“Yeah, be careful. Don’t get hurt, okay?”

Leaving a smile for Emilia, who worried for him until the very end, Subaru stepped out onto the road just as he was sent off.

The silver-haired girl waved her hand in front of the entrance until the mansion was out of sight.

That distant gesture was infinitely endearing, causing the flame in Subaru’s chest, which had been nearly extinguished by anxiety, to blaze up once more.

Alone on the road, he stopped walking after awhile.

Subaru surveyed his surroundings, confirmed there was no sign of anyone, and suddenly stepped off the path and into the forest. The forest flanking the road was deep and connected to the mountains; Ram had strictly warned him not to enter it due to the abundance of wild animals.

Ignoring that warning, Subaru pushed through the vegetation, heading deeper into the woods. He climbed several slopes, maintaining his pace even as protruding branches left scratches on him.

He must have proceeded through the mountains for about fifteen minutes.

“Alright, this is the spot.”

Suddenly the forest opened up, and the high sky filled his widened field of vision. After climbing several slopes, Subaru had arrived at a place like a small, elevated hill nestled in the mountains.

This was his destination. Miming the action of wiping sweat from his brow, Subaru then brought the cliff before him into view—and specifically, the building that existed directly below it.

It was a familiar mansion. None other than the majestic Roswaal estate.

By circling around the road and going through the forest and mountains, he had reached a perfect peeping point from which he could monitor the Roswaal manor from a high vantage. Specifically,

“I can see the west side, where Emilia-tan’s room is, really well. If anything strange happens, I’ll know right away.”

From this distance, Subaru’s eyesight could just faintly make out the window of her room. Even setting that aside, it was a position that allowed him to grasp the full view of the mansion, including the west wing. He judged that if anyone visited the mansion from the outside, he would definitely be able to see them.

It was already past the morning of the fourth day in his third loop. In Subaru’s experience, there were about sixteen hours remaining until the time of his previous death.

Which meant, presumably, that any anomaly at the mansion would occur around then as well.

“Now, I just wait for something to happen.”

If it was only sixteen hours, a stakeout was possible even with Subaru’s mental fortitude.

Ideally, he had wanted to create this situation three days ago—right after the loop started—but he gave himself a three-day buffer, fearing his concentration wouldn’t hold if he acted too hastily.

Thanks to that, his energy, stamina, and motivation were all topped up.

To detect any abnormality at the Roswaal manor in advance, or to create conditions where he could rush in no matter what happened—that was the prerequisite Subaru had prepared.

If he stayed at the mansion and was included in the attacker’s targets from the start, his consciousness would be muddled by the same magic as before.

In the current situation where he wanted even a single fragment of information about the attacker, such a thing would be fatal.

Therefore, Subaru chose a strategy of using Emilia and the others as decoys to lure out the attacker.

Of course, unable to be completely heartless, Subaru had set up several safety lines and intended to dash into the mansion the moment anything happened, running around to warn of the enemy attack.

“It’d help if the enemy is the cautious type who gets spooked and runs when I scream.”

Voicing his optimistic observation, Subaru lowered his tool bag and searched its contents. What he pulled out was a long rope he had “borrowed” from the mansion’s warehouse. From his experience as a servant, he knew exactly where such supplies were kept.

He had sneaked it out when no one was looking, carrying it for just such an emergency.

Tying the rope to the trunk of a nearby thick tree, Subaru secured the other end of the rope to his own body. Of course, using it as a lifeline just like that would kill him from the g-force, so he tied several knots at various points to act as shock absorbers first.

“Now for the small knife to cut the rope… hopefully cutting the rope is all I’ll need it for.”

With a blade length comparable to a fruit knife, he was also considering its role for self-harm in a worst-case scenario.

As a means of resisting the magic from the last time, he could probably crush the initial weakening of his consciousness before it took hold. Though he didn’t think he could counter the debilitation that followed.

“Better than having no plan at all… After all, this time is for preparing countermeasures for the next time.”

Muttering as if to convince himself, Subaru shook his head to banish his timidity.

Suddenly, the faces of the people at the Roswaal manor he had just bid farewell to crossed his mind.

This time, Subaru was trying to use them as sacrificial pawns to prepare for the next loop. Even though, just like the times before, he was supposed to have formed a genuine bond with them.

If he closed his eyes, he could recall the days of these last four days.

He didn’t think he had built as close a relationship with the others this time, but he still had many opportunities to interact with Ram and Rem, and he had actively gone to see Emilia. All while predicting that right now, in this very moment, it would cause his heart to ache like this.

This is a punishment. This is just desserts. This is a penalty he deserves to take.

It is the kind of judgment that Subaru, who planned this strategy on the premise of loss—deciding that he had to use them as pawns at least once—must absolutely accept.

He interacted with them thinking it was painful.

He interacted with them thinking they were dear to him.

Subaru spent these three days enduring the agony of sticking his fingers into an open wound, tearing the flesh further and breaking the bone.

So that he would not forget any of it.

“I told myself this, Natsuki Subaru. When you repeat it, even if everyone else forgets… you will remember.”

That’s why he mustn’t think it’s okay to forget what happens this time.

Until the very, very, very last moment, he must continue to seek the happy ending he desires.

No one has the right to decide that their existence is just bubbles disappearing into the rift of time.

Keeping his body low, clenching his jaw, Subaru hid himself between the trees and grass, monitoring the Roswaal manor through gaps in the forest.

His breathing was shallow, and though his body should have been tense, his heartbeat was strangely slow; he could feel his entire being affirming the resolve Subaru had set.

A sensation of his body obeying him like never before.

While grasping that rare sensation, Subaru waited silently for the time.

※※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※

He lay low, waiting for the time to come.

Tension stiffened his body, anxiety shook his heart unevenly, and impatience caused extraneous things to flicker in his vision.

Quietly avoiding such unconscious interference, Subaru continued to hold his breath.

Six hours had already passed, and the sunset was pouring a brilliant orange into a world that had been before noon.

Thinking back, this was the time when, in previous loops, he would have been heading to the village for shopping with either Ram or Rem.

However, this time he hadn’t confirmed either of them leaving the mansion. Did that mean without Subaru, the shopping event didn’t happen?

“Maybe since there’s one less mouth to feed, purely practical, they pushed the shopping to tomorrow… or something. Weird that I can look at it objectively.”

Because he had been silent for over six hours, the voice he suddenly murmured was hoarser than he expected. Giving a wry smile, Subaru took out the tool bag—and the tube of water inside it—moistening his throat with the cold water. It was simple, like a bamboo tube, but it was a mysterious tool that kept the water inside cold indefinitely. He figured this, too, must be a tool related to magic.

“Just six hours and I’m already this pathetic. It isn’t the time to lose focus. Get it together, man!”

Slapping his cheeks as he spoke, the dry sound snapped his consciousness back into clarity.

There was still nearly half a day left until the predicted time. If he was breaking now, the road ahead looked grim.

He had to shore up his slackening spirit and return to his watch.

Fortunately or unfortunately, it was at the moment Subaru switched his mindset that it happened.

“――――!”

The instant he felt a faint anomaly catch on his eardrum, Subaru’s body leaped to the side without a shred of hesitation.

An evasive maneuver executed exactly as planned, with all senses fully engaged.

It certainly bore fruit, spectacularly saving Subaru’s body from the threat of that surprise attack.

Immediately after, what he heard was the crushing sound of a heavy object snapping a tree in half. The toppling trees swept up everything around them; leaves, branches, and the sound of snapping wood danced wildly.

Subaru bolted through the chaos, instantly throwing himself toward the cliff.

“――――Whaaa!”

Unable to be fully stifled by his clenched teeth, a scream leaked out as he tasted the floating sensation of his insides flipping from the high fall. However after falling only a few meters, his momentum came to an abrupt halt. The rope tied tightly around his waist dug in, and groaning in pain, he gasped,

“Emergency… escape…!”

Saying that, he cut the rope with his knife. His liberated body resumed its fall; where his shoe soles bit into the sloping cliff, and he practically slid down, landing violently on the ground.

Without a moment to catch his breath, Subaru chose to flee, abandoning all appearances. He threw away the tool bag to lighten his load and ran down the mountain with literally just the clothes on his back.

Running out of breath, he shouted,

“I saw it! Haa… Aah! I saw it!”

The object that had mown down the trees—it was a spiked iron ball as big as a person’s embrace. You could call it a bowling ball equipped with killing functions; a romantic weapon connected to its user by a long, long chain—its name: the Morning Star.

The anomaly that had occurred in the mountains was the timbre of the chain connecting that iron ball. That sound, which he remembered hearing, was unmistakably the weapon that had taken Subaru’s life that night.

Having witnessed its power and intimidation, Subaru’s teeth were chattering with belated terror.

If that mass flew at him with sharpness, it wouldn’t be strange for a body taking a direct hit to be blown to pieces. It made perfect sense that his left side had been ripped off.

“But… they came this way!”

Stepping on branches, jumping over ditches, spitting as he conquered the poor footing.

This was an outcome Subaru anticipated. The possibility of him being attacked after he left the mansion was about the same as an attack on the mansion itself.

If they intended to kill everyone involved, Subaru, who had stayed for three days, would hardly vanish from the list. And the fact that they chose Subaru as a target meant,

“Basically, it means they’ve been watching me in that mansion for days.”

The attacker had been monitoring the mansion for several days.

Therefore, they didn’t remove Subaru from the target list even after he left the mansion. Above all, finding Subaru where he lay hidden was the greatest proof.

How could they do that without following Subaru after he left the manor?

“——Wah!”

It was the moment he grew so lost in thought that he neglected his footing.

A tree root caught Subaru’s foot, sending his momentum-carrying body into a spectacular tumble. He rolled across the ground, sliding down the slope. Just then, the iron ball passed overhead as if it had been aimed perfectly.

If he hadn’t been rolling just now— a shiver raced through Subaru’s heart.

He rolled to the side, stood up, spat out the dirt that had gotten into his mouth, and resumed his escape. He had completely lost the path, but he couldn’t stop.

He was out of breath. His lungs hurt. To begin with, Subaru lacked endurance.

He was confident he was above average in all other athletic abilities, but his stamina was truly hopeless. A game of tag on a mountain path—just thinking about it meant he had no chance of winning. If he had no chance just thinking about it, he had even less chance actually doing it.

In other words,

“Being cornered… was inevitable, huh…”

Before him, a cliff towered up as if to imprison Subaru.

The stone wall, revealing hard, sharp fragments, was a natural fortress that refused to be climbed or used as a foothold. Naturally, the current Subaru had no means of overcoming it.

He turned around, took a deep breath in and out, steadied his breathing, before bracing himself.

In front of him, the darkness in the forest had deepened before he knew it, and this place, where the trees obscured the sunset, was filled with a sense of desolation as if cut off from the world.

“If you’re coming… then bring it on…”

Driving away his whining with bravado, Subaru unzipped the front of his jersey and took off the jacket. He spread it out with both hands, taking a stance, and quietly waiting for the attacker to arrive.

He is cornered. He is trapped. Subaru is now nothing more than powerless prey caught in a predator’s trap.

But he won’t just let himself be eaten.

He has sacrificed this much. At the very least, he’s going to get compensation to match.

——In that instant, dragging the sound of chains from beyond the darkness, violence flew at high speed.

“Have you got… the guuuuuuts!?”

Faced with a certain-kill blow, Subaru’s body displayed reflexes that defied common sense.

Lifting the jersey jacket he held in both hands, he wrapped up the incoming iron ball from directly underneath, slightly deflecting its momentum and dodging a direct hit to his torso by a hair’s breadth.

However, the jacket was ripped from his arms, and his body, unable to fully kill the impact, was slammed into the rock wall; he was not unharmed.

But the moment he looked up and saw the iron ball that had missed its mark embedded in the wall, Subaru smiled a smile of supreme satisfaction and firmly grabbed the fully extended chain.

Then, looking toward the opposite end of the stretching chain—the direction where the attacker holding it stood—

“Now show yourself, you piece of shit! I spent a whole week trying to see your face, dammit!”

He raised a roar of anger, emboldening himself by shouting foul curses.

No matter who came out, he strained his eyes and glared into the darkness so he would never miss them.

It was a desperate situation, but somehow he had picked up his life.

Perhaps, without making this loop a sacrificial pawn, it might even be possible to repel the attacker who revealed themselves.

His racing consciousness made Subaru picture thoughts that were indistinguishable from optimism.

In a situation he had once nearly given up on, he desperately reached out for the light he saw.

In that light were Emilia, the twins, the cheeky little girl, and Roswaal. A sensation where he almost forgot the situation and his cheeks nearly relaxed, and then,

“——I suppose it can’t be helped.”

The sound of chains rang out, and he felt the slack as the owner approached.

However leaving such trivial sensations behind, Subaru’s eyes were wide open.

His lips trembled, and a voiceless voice leaked from his throat as a groan.

Unconsciously, his fingers let go of the chain they grasped, and his head shook slightly, weakly from side to side as if rejecting it.

Treading on grass, stepping over branches, her figure slowly emerged from the darkness.

An apron dress based in black, a pure white headdress adorning her head. Gripping the handle of the chain connected to the iron ball—a weapon that completely mismatched her petite frame—

“It would have been best if you had simply met your end without realizing anything.”

Swaying her blue hair, tilting her head with that familiar expressionless look,

“You’re kidding… Rem.”

The girl he thought he wanted to protect was raising a flail before him.
